definitions.missing_row: Parent id × one of de/en/ru/uk/tr has no translation row; optional help rows are not necessarily required.
definitions.blank_fields: Existing rows only: NULL, empty strings and whitespace-only strings; optional fields are counted separately.
definitions.required_blank_fields: Non-German vocabulary translation, context_sentence for sentence_practice cards, and course title; an audit convention, not a new database constraint.
definitions.source_field_missing: Non-German field is blank or the row is missing, while its corresponding German source is nonblank.
definitions.no_cyrillic_rows: Nonblank ru/uk row with no Cyrillic in any inspected text field. Empty rows are counted only as empty, not twice.
definitions.exact_german_copy: Nonblank corresponding field equals de byte-for-byte; no case folding, trimming or fuzzy language detection.
definitions.canonical_german_sources: If de translation text is absent, vocabulary translation uses learning_vocabulary_cards.word_de, and course title/description use courses.title/description. Raw de row/blank counts are still reported.
definitions.optional_prompt: grammar_translations.prompt is read via to_jsonb, audited when present in the schema, otherwise recorded as unavailable_fields; missing source-backed prompts are counted.
definitions.heuristic_limits: Names, international words, quoted German examples and empty optional hints/descriptions are not automatically translation errors. English is not covered by the requested Cyrillic/copy heuristics.
definitions.german_scope: Exercise topic and string leaves under instruction, text_before, text_after, question, correct_answer, gap_hint, options, accepted_answers, parts, target_form; reading sentence_de/focus. Localized hints, smart_hint, explanations and translation prompts are excluded, matching migration 07.
definitions.forbidden_characters: After Unicode NFC: Cyrillic U+0400–052F, U+1C80–1C8F, U+1D2B, U+1D78, U+2DE0–2DFF, U+A640–A69F, U+1E030–1E08F and ı ğ ş İ Ğ Ş; zero matches does not prove German language.

text_fields.hint: Im Gegensatz zum Russischen (wo das Verb "sein" im Präsens oft weggelassen wird), muss im Deutschen immer ein Verb stehen: "Ich BIN Nico."
Im Deutschen ist "Mädchen" sächlich (das), da es ein Diminutiv (-chen) ist, unabhängig vom natürlichen Geschlecht.
